correctness.rationale: Every subalgebra is classified by its image \(U\) in \(L_q/Z(L_q)\), its central kernel \(C\), and a graph map \(U\to Z/C\). The three projection dimensions give exactly \(q+3\), \(2q^3+3q^2+2q+1\), and \(q^2+1\) subalgebras. The permutability criterion reduces failure to distinct projection lines and \(z\notin C+D\), whose weighted graph count is \(q^3(3q+1)\) per ordered line pair. A standalone exhaustive enumeration over \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(\mathbb F_3\) independently reproduces both total and bad-pair counts. The arbitrary-\(q\) theorem rests on the symbolic count, not the finite checks.

value.rationale: The object is the first central stabilization of the source paper’s basic nonabelian Heisenberg example, so it is a natural structural perturbation rather than an arbitrary slice. The exact formula shows a qualitative asymptotic change: the unstabilized Heisenberg degree tends to \(0\), while one central dimension produces limit \(1/4\). The proof also gives the complete subalgebra count and isolates precisely which central graph data cause nonpermutability, information useful for extending the invariant to degenerate alternating forms.
